problem_type: Lane resources retained after cleanup failure
symptom: A failed session close leaves the project repository holder and native sandbox alive after the workspace has closed.
direct_cause: Cleanup awaits run sequentially without finally; a transcript or session error skips all later resource releases.
class_root: Owned resources are released only along the successful close path.
internal_only_reason: Nomi owns the nesting of pi session, repository and native sandbox resources. Public SDK fault-injection fixtures reproduce the skipped release.
invariants: Every owned resource receives its close or release attempt even if an earlier cleanup rejects.
Closing failures still reject; resource release does not convert them into success.
generality_proof: Finally boundaries cover both live and read-only handles and their construction failures, independent of the underlying storage failure.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Unwind native resources and repository ownership on all live lane close paths.
Release history repository ownership even if session cleanup fails.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Session or approval-note failure cannot skip native close and repository release.
Both session cleanup paths release repository ownership in finally.

recurrence.reason: Any storage or hook failure can reject a cleanup await before later resources are released.
same_class_scan: Inspected openLane assemble catch and close.
Inspected openLaneHistory construction catch and close; checked laneSession repository holder ownership.

prevention.invariant: Resource ownership is unwound on success and failure.
prevention.failure_mode: Close rejects while finally still attempts every remaining owned release.
prevention.strategy: Use nested finally at the existing resource owners without adding a parallel lifecycle manager.

legacy_paths.rationale: Existing close owners are repaired in place; no alternate lifecycle implementation exists.

dependency_lifecycle.target: A supported pi version preserving explicit session and repository close ownership.
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Rejected cleanup is an ordinary public API outcome; the application must unwind its own resources.
exit_criteria: Rerun public session-close fault fixtures whenever pi changes close ownership or error propagation.

residual_risks: A resource may itself fail to close; this change guarantees every close is attempted and errors remain visible.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The existing lane handle owns the SDK and sandbox lifetimes, so its finally boundary must release them.
